results.name: medium-stp-off-baseline
results.title: Baseline · all bridges STP off
results.action: Reset the data bridge on all three CHRs over management SSH with protocol-mode=none (priority 0x1000 on both MLAG peers, 0x8000 on the access switch). Then run numbered 100 ms pings for 4 s in both VLAN 110 directions and both bypass directions, read back bridge, MLAG and LACP state, and send three ARP broadcasts each way. No fault is applied.

results.name: medium-stp-off-power-loss-secondary
results.title: MLAG secondary power loss · Medium lab, all bridges STP off
results.action: Resets all three bridges over management SSH with protocol-mode=none. It requires a loss-free probe baseline, zero BPDUs and one copy of each broadcast. It then emulates a power loss of CHR 2 (MLAG secondary, mlag-priority=20): in one step it takes the container veths behind CHR 2's ether2 to ether4 down, sets the facing NICs of CHR 1 and the access switch link-down over QMP and pauses CHR 2's guest with QMP stop, then confirms carrier loss at every neighbour. After 20 s it powers CHR 2 on with QMP system_reset and cont, brings the links back up, waits for the guest uptime to reset and keeps probing for 16 s plus a 3 s recovery window.

witness.name: dc1-access-switch1
witness.role: Dual-attached access switch and external RSTP root candidate

c1.name: dc1-traffic-host1
c1.role: Linux VLAN 110 and bypass probe host 1

c2.name: dc1-traffic-host2
c2.role: Linux VLAN 110 and bypass probe host 2

outside_delivery.status: not applicable: the Medium lab has no host outside the conversation

phases.name: Secondary off
phases.expected: Every link to CHR 2 loses carrier at once, as on a real power loss. CHR 1 (MLAG primary) sees its peer port ether2 go down and keeps the shared system ID, so the access switch's uplink bond and traffic host 2 keep their LACP partner. They drop their member to CHR 2 on carrier loss, without waiting for the LACP short timeout, and forward over their members to CHR 1. With protocol-mode=none no port changes state and no BPDUs appear.

phases.name: Secondary back
phases.expected: Carrier returns while CHR 2 boots. CHR 2 keeps its bond members out of the 802.3ad bond until the MLAG system ID syncs with CHR 1 (mlag-init-delay), then adds them under the unchanged shared system ID. The access switch and traffic host 2 re-add the member to the same aggregator, so loss is brief or none.

results.name: medium-stp-off-power-loss-primary
results.title: MLAG primary power loss · Medium lab, all bridges STP off
results.action: Resets all three bridges over management SSH with protocol-mode=none. It requires a loss-free probe baseline, zero BPDUs and one copy of each broadcast. It then emulates a power loss of CHR 1 (MLAG primary, mlag-priority=10): in one step it takes the container veths behind CHR 1's ether2 to ether4 down, sets the facing NICs of CHR 2 and the access switch link-down over QMP and pauses CHR 1's guest with QMP stop, then confirms carrier loss at every neighbour. After 20 s it powers CHR 1 on with QMP system_reset and cont, brings the links back up, waits for the guest uptime to reset and keeps probing for 16 s plus a 3 s recovery window.

witness.role: Dual-attached access switch and external RSTP root candidate

c1.role: Linux VLAN 110 and bypass probe host 1

phases.name: Primary off
phases.expected: Every link to CHR 1 loses carrier at once, as on a real power loss. CHR 2 sees its peer port ether2 go down and reverts its MLAG bonds to its own LACP system ID, so the access switch and traffic host 2 renegotiate LACP, with brief loss. They drop their member to CHR 1 on carrier loss, without waiting for the LACP short timeout. With protocol-mode=none no port changes state and no BPDUs appear.

phases.name: Primary back
phases.expected: Carrier returns while CHR 1 boots. CHR 1 keeps its bond members out of the bond until the MLAG system ID syncs (mlag-init-delay), rejoins as MLAG primary and restores the shared system ID. The access switch and traffic host 2 renegotiate LACP to the shared system ID, with brief loss.
